sections.title: 1. What Software Architecture Is and What Architects Do
sections.template:
## 1. What Software Architecture Is and What Architects Do

**Lab:** Describe your system's architecture in one page

**Task 1.** List five to eight building blocks of your system, each with a one-sentence responsibility.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Draw or list the relations between the blocks, naming what flows along each relation.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Write two decision records of three to five lines each, with context, choice, one alternative and one consequence.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Name who currently does each architect task (clarify requirements, design, decide, communicate, check) and mark any task with no owner.

_Your answer._

**Task 5.** Pick one misconception from this lesson and describe where you saw it in your project.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The block list, the relations, two decision records, the task owner table, and one sentence on the misconception.

sections.title: 2. Stakeholders, Requirements and Constraints
sections.template:
## 2. Stakeholders, Requirements and Constraints

**Lab:** Requirements and constraints sheet

**Task 1.** Build a stakeholder table with at least six stakeholders and their main concerns.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Write three functional requirements and, for each, one quality requirement with a number or a clear test.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** List at least four constraints and label each as technical, organisational or regulatory with its origin.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Write five assumptions, each with an owner and how you would check it.

_Your answer._

**Task 5.** Name two conflicting goals between stakeholders and state who must decide between them.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The stakeholder table, the requirement pairs, the constraint list with origins, the assumption list with owners, and the conflict note.

sections.title: 3. Quality Attributes and Measurable Scenarios
sections.template:
## 3. Quality Attributes and Measurable Scenarios

**Lab:** Write three measurable quality scenarios

**Task 1.** Rank the top three to five quality attributes for your system and give one sentence of reasoning for each.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Write three scenarios, each with source, stimulus, environment, artefact, response and response measure.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Replace every vague word in a sample requirement with a figure or an observable behaviour.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** State a baseline or, if unknown, how you would measure it, for each scenario.

_Your answer._

**Task 5.** Name one trade-off between two of your scenarios and say what you would give up.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The ranked list, three six-part scenarios, the rewritten requirement, baselines or measurement plans, and the trade-off note.

sections.title: 4. Design Approaches and Decomposition
sections.template:
## 4. Design Approaches and Decomposition

**Lab:** Context, blocks and a requirements-to-blocks table

**Task 1.** List the people and systems that interact with your system and say in one line what each exchanges with it.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Name five to nine first-level building blocks and write one sentence of responsibility for each.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Make a table of your five most important requirements and name the block that fulfils each one.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Pick the single riskiest decision and describe a one-day check (prototype, measurement or review) that would give feedback on it.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The context list, the blocks with responsibilities, the requirements-to-blocks table and the plan for one feedback check.

sections.title: 5. Design Principles and Patterns
sections.template:
## 5. Design Principles and Patterns

**Lab:** Choose principles and a pattern, with reasons

**Task 1.** List the three decisions in your system most likely to change and the interface that will hide each one.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Find two dependencies that cross block borders without an interface and say how you would fix each.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Choose one architectural pattern for the whole system and write the requirement it serves, the benefit and the cost.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Name one principle you decided to relax and the requirement that justifies it.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The change list with interfaces, two dependency fixes, the pattern with its three lines and the relaxed principle with its reason.

sections.title: 6. Interfaces, Contracts and Data Models
sections.template:
## 6. Interfaces, Contracts and Data Models

**Lab:** Write one interface and map dependencies and data owners

**Task 1.** Write an interface description for one block with its purpose, operations, inputs, outputs and error cases in a table.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Draw or list the dependencies between your blocks and mark any cycle or shortcut around an interface.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** List your five most important data items and name the one block that owns each.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Name one change to the interface that would break callers and describe how you would roll it out safely.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The interface table, the dependency list with problems marked, the data-owner table and the safe change plan.

sections.title: 7. Runtime Views and Distributed Systems
sections.template:
## 7. Runtime Views and Distributed Systems

**Lab:** Write two runtime scenarios with failure paths

**Task 1.** Write the main scenario for your system as numbered steps naming the blocks involved in order.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Write a failure scenario for one external dependency and state what the user sees and what the system does.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Identify one operation that must be safe to retry and describe how a repeat is recognised.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** State one piece of data that must be consistent at once and one that may catch up, with a reason for each.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** Two numbered scenarios, the retry rule, and the two consistency decisions with reasons.

sections.title: 8. Deployment and Infrastructure
sections.template:
## 8. Deployment and Infrastructure

**Lab:** Draw the deployment view and review it

**Task 1.** List the nodes your system runs on and which building blocks run on each.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** List your environments and say what data each one holds.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Find every single point of failure and say whether your requirements accept it or not.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Write two operations needs, for example backup and rollback, and say how the design provides each one.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The node list with blocks, the environment table, the single points of failure with decisions and the two operations needs.

sections.title: 9. Cross-Cutting Concepts
sections.template:
## 9. Cross-Cutting Concepts

**Lab:** Write the cross-cutting concepts page

**Task 1.** List at least five concerns that touch more than one building block in your system.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** For each concern write a one or two sentence rule that every block must follow.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Choose one concern and write an example showing the rule in use.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** For one concern describe a check, such as a test or review step, that shows the rule is followed.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The concern list, the rules, one example and one check.

sections.title: 10. Documenting and Communicating Architecture
sections.template:
## 10. Documenting and Communicating Architecture

**Lab:** Plan your documentation and write two decision records

**Task 1.** List three readers of your architecture documentation and the three questions each one needs answered.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Choose the views you will provide and say which reader and which question each view serves.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Write a decision record for one important decision with its context, the decision, two alternatives and the consequences.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Write a second record for a decision that was hard to reverse, and note the review date or trigger for revisiting it.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The readers and questions, the view list, and two decision records.

sections.title: 11. Analysing and Assessing Architecture
sections.template:
## 11. Analysing and Assessing Architecture

**Lab:** Plan an architecture analysis

**Task 1.** Write the question your analysis should answer and say when in the project it is cheapest to ask it.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Choose three quality scenarios with measurable responses that the analysis will test.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** For each scenario name the evidence you would collect and state one limit of that evidence.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Write two risks that you expect to find, each with impact, owner and a decision to fix, accept or investigate.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The analysis question, three scenarios, the evidence and its limits, and two risks with owners.

sections.title: 12. Worked Example: The Integrated Case Study
sections.template:
## 12. Worked Example: The Integrated Case Study

**Lab:** Trace three requirements end to end

**Task 1.** Choose three important requirements or constraints, at least one of them a quality requirement, and write each as a concern and a requirement.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** For each, name the decision that answers it and the best alternative you rejected with the reason.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** For each, name the view where the decision appears and the code or test that realises it.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** List every missing link in the three chains as a task, each with an owner.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** Three chains in a table, and a task list for the missing links.

sections.title: 13. AI-Assisted Architecture Work
sections.template:
## 13. AI-Assisted Architecture Work

**Lab:** Write your AI-use rules and verify one draft

**Task 1.** Write five rules for AI use in your architecture work, covering allowed tasks, forbidden data, verification and accountability.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Take a short draft text about your system, from an assistant or written by hand, and list every technical claim in it.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** For each claim write how you would verify it and what the authoritative source is, and mark it verified, wrong or unknown.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Write a provenance note for the document that says what was generated, what was checked and who is accountable.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The five rules, the claim table and the provenance note.

sections.title: 14. Exam Strategy and the Final Mock
sections.template:
## 14. Exam Strategy and the Final Mock

**Lab:** Build your exam plan from a mock result

**Task 1.** Record your mock score, your score for each chapter and the time you used, and note the chapter that was weakest.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** List three questions you got wrong or guessed and trace each one to a lesson and a learning goal.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Write a revision plan for the next two weeks that names the lessons you will revisit and when you will take the next mock.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Write your one page exam-day plan: pacing marks, how you handle flagged questions, and the rules you need to check with the certification body.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The mock numbers, the three traced questions, the revision plan and the exam-day plan.
